This implies a possible regulatory mechanism where Isatin may influence the activity of these channels through its interaction with the cationic amino acid transporter 2. The presence of a high confidence score in the pathway suggests that the relationship is well-supported, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be elucidated. The integration of these entities highlights a potential role for Isatin in modulating calcium channel function, possibly through the transport of cationic molecules that affect channel activity.
